- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.4) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast peak at 1–2% above prior high.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is falling, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature bottoming.  
- If 3–5 consecutive days of low sentiment and forecast is trending up, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast to align with mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (especially after 10–15 days), reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect lagged market reaction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive and forecast is high, apply a 1–2% downward bias to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
